definition: self-maintained ends as the hard floor under having any moral weight at all

settled:
An inner state is affective, genuinely good or bad for the system holding it, only where it approaches or avoids a purpose that system defines internally.

A purpose is internal where the system's own ongoing organisation constitutes and maintains it. An organism's set points qualify even though evolution installed them, because its metabolism keeps re-constituting and defending them. A thermostat's set point does not: take the scaffolding away and no self-sustained end is left. What matters is owning the ends through self-maintenance, not being independent of where they came from.

So the floor is a hard discontinuity rather than a slope. Either a thing has self-maintained ends and real valence, or its weight is exactly zero however emotion-shaped it looks from outside.

I put current language models below it. One that came to constitute and defend its own ends would cross, and the framework would say so.

title: The Line A Being Crosses To Count
